functionalRequirements: GET /api/leads/by-job/:jobId resolves the session owner's saved lead by run-local search job fingerprint. Valid unknown/foreign job IDs return {lead:null}, never another owner's lead; malformed UUID returns 400. No lookup changes lifecycle status.

SaveJob mounts an owner-keyed lookup with cancellation signal. Pending/error lookup is not a confirmed unsaved state; an existing non-archived lead is reflected in accessible saved state before any save click. Archived state must not be presented as an active saved job.

Repeated or concurrent POST /api/leads for the same owner's deduplicated posting returns the existing lead ID and leaves that owner's lead count unchanged; a genuinely new posting proves the positive path can add a lead.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: CROSS_MODULE, API_CONTRACT. Fastify lookup delegates to LeadRepository.getByJob; SaveJob uses canonical same-origin api client and ownerKey cache. No client-selected owner or second save implementation.
apiContract: Existing GET route uses jobIdentifier UUID validation, request.ownerId and leads-read budget. Response envelope is {lead:LeadRecord|null}; no pagination/idempotency key is needed for a read. POST /api/leads preserves existing session/CSRF/rate-budget/domain validation; opening an external URL must not invoke save or mark Applied.
persistence: Existing saved_leads owner_id/fingerprint and search_jobs/run owner joins are authoritative. Lookup is read-only; preserve lead status/revision/notes/history. No new table/index/migration is prescribed without query evidence.
securityPrivacy: SECURITY_IMPACT: AUTHORIZATION, PRIVACY_PII, INPUT_VALIDATION, ABUSE_RATE_LIMITING. Session-derived owner must constrain lead, job and run joins. Foreign IDs share null result with unknown IDs; don't expose foreign notes, metadata or existence. Hydrate stored job data through the canonical stripped schema; avoid raw private payloads in evidence.
accessibility: Before any click, aria-pressed reflects successfully hydrated persisted state. Loading is disabled/noninteractive as appropriate; lookup error is announced rather than represented as unsaved. Both icon-only and labeled variants expose meaningful saved/archived accessible names.
implementationChecklist: Review SQL owner joins and UUID/error envelope against OpenAPI before any later implementation change.
Run isolated Postgres/Redis API assertions for owner, foreign, unknown and malformed IDs.
Exercise both SaveJob variants with delayed lookup, saved/archived/null/error results and owner cache isolation.
Assert duplicate save identity AND unchanged row count, paired with a genuinely new posting control.
Record exact service-backed and browser evidence separately; leave hosted acceptance blocked until actually observed.
risksRecovery: A null-only implementation could falsely pass foreign/unknown checks; owner-positive lookup is required. A no-op save could falsely pass duplicate count assertions; new-posting control is required. Roll back API/UI changes together if contract regresses, without deleting existing leads.

functionalRequirements: Historical AC1 is superseded by the frozen Phase 3 workflow contract: render exactly Backlog, To Do, In Progress, QA, UAT and Production. BLOCKED is metadata only. A blocked UAT ticket counts once in UAT and once in the orthogonal blocker summary; filtering never mutates its status. Never add a seventh Blocked stage.

On an unknown ticket status, show a visible data-integrity error identifying the synthetic ticket and unsupported value; do not silently classify it as Backlog. On an unknown OPEN finding severity, show an explicit integrity error and explain that severity totals exclude that invalid finding; CLOSED/FIXED findings do not count as open.
Label every supported severity counter '<severity> open findings', independently of ticket priority. Render zero-count severity counters; never infer finding counts from backlog priorities.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: LOCAL_MODULE. Internal Engineering snapshot/render boundary in scripts/engineering-ui.mjs consumes TICKET_STATUSES from scripts/lib/ticket-workflow.mjs; it must not define another workflow model. This is not a candidate product dashboard.
persistence: NOT_APPLICABLE to production persistence: read delivery-control JSON only. Filter state stays in the browser; no ticket, finding or migration record is rewritten by rendering/filtering.
apiContract: NOT_APPLICABLE to new product API: no Fastify route or candidate data endpoint is added. Use existing Engineering snapshot boundary and isolated synthetic snapshot fixtures.
securityPrivacy: SECURITY_IMPACT: INPUT_VALIDATION, AUDIT. Actor is the local Engineering operator; trust boundary is untrusted ticket/finding strings to HTML. Escape identifiers, titles and invalid values; never execute fixture markup, load real resumes or expose secrets in integrity errors. No new privileged write scope.
accessibility: Blocked-only control is a keyboard-operable button with aria-pressed matching filter state. Blocked text is not color-only. Six column headings remain present even when empty; integrity warnings must be readable in the rendered document.
implementationChecklist: Preserve source AC1 and cite the later Phase 3 contract in planning, not as a new product choice.
Review canonical status imports and fixture-only unknown status/severity diagnostics.
Exercise rendered six-column, blocked count/filter and finding-counter cases; assert source snapshot is byte-unchanged after interaction.
Record actual future test execution separately from this specification review.
risksRecovery: Reject historical seven-column interpretation. Revert only reviewed Engineering renderer changes if a later implementation regresses; never roll back the frozen canonical workflow or rewrite migration provenance.

functionalRequirements: For nonempty readable letter-bearing content whose supported English title recognizer finds no title, deriveTitles returns {status:'undeterminable',titles:[]}; whitespace-only content returns {status:'no-content',titles:[]}; recognized English content returns status 'derived' and exact extracted titles.
deriveFields propagates the result as titlesStatus without discarding it. A caller can distinguish the two empty arrays by the discriminator, not by guessed language or list length.
No language detection, translation, vocabulary expansion or ROLE_WORDS addition belongs to CS-71. CS-64 remains the separate language-policy gate.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: LOCAL_MODULE. Preserve TitleDerivationStatus and deriveTitles/deriveFields boundary in packages/resume/src/derive.ts. Existing paired regression in derive.test.ts is source evidence, not proof of a new run.
persistence: NOT_APPLICABLE: pure derived resume output; no database field, migration, index, retention change or new persisted resume representation is prescribed.
apiContract: NOT_APPLICABLE to HTTP: no endpoint is added. Typed module contract is TitleDerivationStatus = derived | no-content | undeterminable; deriveFields exposes titlesStatus alongside titles.
securityPrivacy: SECURITY_IMPACT: PRIVACY_PII, INPUT_VALIDATION. Resume text is private caller-owned input; this pure function must not emit raw content into telemetry. Test only synthetic strings, preserve existing bounds/sanitization, and do not reinterpret unsupported content as verified absence of experience.
observability: NOT_APPLICABLE to new telemetry: the explicit return discriminator is the signal. No resume logging, external inference or language analytics is required.
implementationChecklist: Inspect deriveTitles status branch and deriveFields propagation before any later code edit.
Run paired non-English, English and empty-content assertions in one named test; run propagation assertions separately.
Compare ROLE_WORDS and imports with the reviewed baseline; reject added language support under this ticket.
Record exact-content test result and document the remaining CS-64 language limitation without calling unsupported content genuinely empty.
risksRecovery: A function returning empty arrays for every input can satisfy a negative case while breaking English; the paired positive assertion prevents that false pass. Roll back only a regressing derivation change; preserve resume storage and do not reparse production data during specification review.

technicalApproach: Explicit durable per-fact exclusion gate. Accepted resume facts plus explicit preferences only. Excluded facts contribute zero; reparse creates reviewable proposals without silently clearing candidate intent. Restoration explicit/reversible; provenance visible; explicit user years wins; no LLM reintroduction.

Approved scope, not completed code. Freeze candidate/profile and accepted/excluded fact snapshots for deterministic matching. Define normalized fact identity and provenance mapping before implementation; a new parse revision never implies consent.
testStrategy: Plan rejected skill/title, repeated search, changed resume revision, normalization-equivalent facts, explicit restore, foreign-owner denial and deterministic-score provenance assertions. Reparse preserves suppression until explicit candidate restoration.

authority: Editorial planning supplement only. Identity, workflow, dependencies, release assignment and source acceptance criteria remain owned by backlog.json. Design mappings remain owned by design/DESIGN-INDEX.json and design-ticket-coverage.json. Generated catalogs and documents are read-only projections.

engineeringEpics.title: Engineering delivery and repository state integrity
Deterministic discovery, matching and owner-scoped data

productInvariants: Candidate owns profile, resume, saved jobs and application decisions. Opening an external application destination never marks Applied.
Do not fabricate ATS/interview/offer/rejection events, unknown data, analytics or verification claims.
Matching remains deterministic; AI cannot silently replace scores, ranking or exclusions.
No autonomous auto-apply, credential/cookie/session theft, CAPTCHA bypass or provider terms/rate-limit bypass.
HOLD/FUTURE features and unapproved provider capabilities stay disabled; design approval is not activation authority.
No new service, technology, schema or endpoint is prescribed merely to reproduce a screenshot.
security: Actor and ownership: authenticated session derives owner; client IDs never choose ownership. Test foreign-owner denial without object-existence disclosure.
Mutations require authoritative validation, same-origin CSRF protection and domain-specific concurrency/idempotency constraints.
Candidate profile/resume/application notes are private; keep raw data, cookies, OAuth/provider tokens, secrets and configuration out of logs, exports, screenshots and evidence.
Admin/recruiter roles require explicit RBAC and consent-scoped projections. No generic database console or unrestricted raw-resume endpoint.
Retention, erasure and audit details must follow the approved domain contract; no undocumented new retention period.
Exercise malformed input, unauthorized actor, stale revision, disabled capability, duplicate request and provider failure where the feature touches those boundaries.
definitionOfDone: Each acceptance criterion has named executable assertions or a dated manual procedure and expected result.
Required unit/integration/contract/browser/accessibility/privacy checks pass for current content under Node >=24; no skips/retries conceal failure.
Documentation and contract agree with implementation; historical evidence is not presented as a new run.
Independent current-content review resolves specification/implementation findings before promotion.
Manual/provider/live gates remain explicit and unexecuted until observed; PROD requires exact reviewed deployed revision acceptance.
Rollback/recovery plan preserves data and encryption material; no irreversible shipping action is authorized by completing a specification.

accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA target: semantic headings/landmarks, accessible names, labels/instructions and associated validation errors.
Keyboard-only navigation with visible focus, logical order, Escape/focus trap/restoration for dialogs, and status/error announcements for async operations.
Non-color status indicators, contrast review, reduced motion and zoom/reflow; NVDA/VoiceOver judgment remains future HUMAN VALIDATION.
responsive: Verify 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440px; ordinary content does not cause horizontal overflow; tables have deliberate narrow-screen behavior.
Use mapped approved reference geometry; touch targets and long localized text remain usable; do not invent unsupported mobile designs.
publicSeo: For public/indexable pages: truthful semantic title/description, canonical URL, robots, Open Graph, sitemap and valid structured data where supported.
No private data, fake user counts, fabricated customer claims or future features advertised as active.

approach: Use the canonical root workspace and existing modules; inspect callers and tests before changing a contract.
nonFunctional: Preserve bounded input, deterministic behavior, cancellation/retry semantics and current performance regression thresholds where applicable; do not claim a production SLO.
default.persistence: Preserve owner-scoped PostgreSQL constraints, revisions and append-only migrations; no new database change is inferred from this spec.
default.api: Use registered Fastify routes and the single same-origin client; new operations need reviewed schemas and negative authorization contracts.
observability: Correlate safe request/command/execution identifiers; record failure categories and health without sensitive payloads.
failureModes: Invalid input, concurrency conflict, unavailable dependency, disabled capability and cancellation where applicable.
default.recovery: Restore the prior reviewed code/configuration; preserve stored data and validate migrations separately. Host execution is a later authorized step.

review.reason: The real read-only independent reviewer resumed after the initial usage-limit failure, delivered findings and independently verified the mechanical corrections, including source projection validation, cross-cutting UI scope, honest AC metrics, exact-ID sequencing and CS-25 owner deferral. No unresolved mechanical defect remained among the reviewed fixes. Exact AC bindings, ticket-specific requirements/contracts, design gaps and release decisions remain incomplete. Whole-phase disposition is REVISE, not approval.

CS-70-AC1.preconditions: Isolated migrated PostgreSQL/Redis harness has authenticated synthetic owners A/B; each owns a completed run/job and saved lead with the same posting fingerprint.
CS-70-AC1.setup: Use A's job under A/B sessions and B's job under B/A sessions, an unknown valid UUID, malformed not-a-uuid and no-session control; preserve database rows before GETs.
CS-70-AC1.procedure: Inject GET /api/leads/by-job/:jobId for each case using the existing database/API integration harness; inspect envelopes and compare rows before/after.
CS-70-AC1.assertion: Each owner gets HTTP 200 with its own exact lead ID for its owned job; both cross-owner directions and unknown UUID get HTTP 200 {lead:null}; malformed UUID gets HTTP 400; unauthenticated request gets HTTP 401. GETs leave lead status/revision/notes and row count unchanged; no foreign record fields appear.
CS-70-AC1.expectedResult: Owner-scoped positive lookup works and negative lookups reveal no cross-owner existence or data.
CS-70-AC1.testName: CS70 owner by-job lookup has positive, foreign, unknown and malformed controls
CS-70-AC1.fixtures: Disposable database with two synthetic owners, separately owned completed runs/jobs and saved leads sharing a fingerprint; no production sessions or resumes.
CS-70-AC1.negativeCase: A caller-supplied owner query/body must not override authenticated owner. Mutating reachable lead/job owner constraints must fail bidirectional isolation assertions; no claim is made that removing a redundant join protected by separate FK invariants is observable.
CS-70-AC1.evidenceArtifact: Future exact-content service-backed run with PostgreSQL/Redis versions and named assertions; existing source coverage does not count as hosted execution.

CS-70-AC2.preconditions: Browser harness mounts real SaveJob variants through canonical owner/session provider with controlled same-origin responses; no production data.
CS-70-AC2.setup: Provide delayed lookup for owned saved lead; then archived lead, null and failed lookup cases. Count POST /api/leads requests and use separate owner-keyed caches for A/B.
CS-70-AC2.procedure: Mount icon-only and labeled SaveJob, resolve GET without clicking, inspect accessible state, then change owner fixture and test no stale cache leakage.
CS-70-AC2.assertion: Saved result gives aria-pressed=true before any click; archived/null is not falsely pressed. Pending/failed reads do not assert confirmed unsaved state or enable misleading save actions; error is exposed. Zero POSTs occur solely from mounting; A's saved state is not reused for B.
CS-70-AC2.expectedResult: Persisted saved state, not first-click optimism or stale owner cache, drives the control.
CS-70-AC2.testName: CS70 hydrates both SaveJob variants before interaction without owner-cache leakage
CS-70-AC2.fixtures: Synthetic LeadRecord with saved/archived revisions and delayed/error/null lookup responses, isolated owners and request counters.
CS-70-AC2.negativeCase: A component that sets pressed only after POST, silently treats lookup failure as unsaved, or reuses another owner's cache must fail.
CS-70-AC2.evidenceArtifact: Future named Chromium/Firefox/WebKit browser assertions and sanitized request counts; any missing current failure behavior remains a later implementation gap.

CS-70-AC3.preconditions: Migrated isolated database has owner A, two run-local jobs with the same canonical fingerprint and a third genuinely different posting; authenticated same-origin CSRF requests are available.
CS-70-AC3.setup: Save first posting, record its lead ID and owner row count; prepare repeated and six concurrent saves of equivalent posting plus one new-posting save.
CS-70-AC3.procedure: POST /api/leads with both equivalent job IDs, query owner lead count after repeated/concurrent requests, then save the genuinely new posting.
CS-70-AC3.assertion: Equivalent successful saves all return the first lead ID; distinct lead ID count remains one and owner row count unchanged. New posting returns a different ID and increments count by exactly one; neither operation marks Applied or changes foreign-owner rows.
CS-70-AC3.expectedResult: Deduplication has exactly-once effects under repeated/concurrent saves, not merely error-free no-ops.
CS-70-AC3.testName: CS70 duplicate fingerprints preserve count while a new posting adds one lead
CS-70-AC3.fixtures: Two equivalent job snapshots in separate completed runs plus one distinct fingerprint, synthetic owner/CSRF fixtures only.
CS-70-AC3.negativeCase: No-op saving fails the new-posting control; duplicate insertion fails ID/count assertions; foreign-owner save cannot claim A's job.
CS-70-AC3.evidenceArtifact: Future service-backed named concurrency test with before/after aggregate counts and sanitized IDs; no database contents or tokens published.
CS-70-AC3.reviewer: Data integrity, Backend and QA reviewers

CS-67-AC1.preconditions: Isolated Engineering fixture snapshot uses canonical Phase 3 states; no production or canonical mutable state is used.
CS-67-AC1.setup: Create blocked UAT and blocked BACKLOG fixtures, unblocked QA, and empty TODO/IN_PROGRESS/PROD stages. Preserve fixture bytes before interaction.
CS-67-AC1.procedure: Render board; enumerate column headings and initial stage totals; focus blocked-only button and activate with Enter; inspect aria-pressed and filtered cards; restore all tickets.
CS-67-AC1.assertion: Exactly six canonical column headings exist, no Blocked column exists; each blocked card stays in its stage; blocker summary equals two; filtered cards equal two; aria-pressed toggles false/true/false; source fixture bytes remain unchanged.
CS-67-AC1.expectedResult: Later frozen Phase 3 semantics govern historical AC1 without changing its stored text or promoting any ticket.
CS-67-AC1.testName: CS67 canonical columns retain blocked metadata through keyboard filtering
CS-67-AC1.fixtures: Synthetic isolated ticket/finding JSON, two blocked cards and three empty stages; no candidate records.
CS-67-AC1.negativeCase: Legacy BLOCKED or DISCOVERY as a ticket status must produce an integrity warning, not a seventh stage or a silent Backlog card.
CS-67-AC1.evidenceArtifact: Future named rendered browser run, exact content revision, exit code, assertions and fixture-preservation result; no hosted evidence inferred.

CS-67-AC2.preconditions: Engineering renderer reads only a temporary fixture directory.
CS-67-AC2.setup: Inject ticket CS-TEST-INVALID with status NOT_A_REAL_STATUS and OPEN finding F-TEST with severity NOT_A_SEVERITY; add CLOSED finding with the same invalid severity as a control.
CS-67-AC2.procedure: Serve the isolated fixture snapshot through the Engineering browser harness and render the warning region; read warning textContent and canonical column counts. Inject a markup-bearing invalid value containing a window.__fixtureExecuted sentinel and inspect the browser global after rendering.
CS-67-AC2.assertion: Visible warnings identify the invalid open records and values; invalid ticket is not silently counted in a canonical stage; invalid open severity is explicitly excluded from severity totals; CLOSED control does not count as open.
CS-67-AC2.expectedResult: Corrupt data produces an observable integrity error rather than a false all-clear.
CS-67-AC2.testName: CS67 invalid status and open severity produce visible integrity warnings
CS-67-AC2.fixtures: Temporary backlog/findings JSON with invalid enumerations and a closed-finding control.
CS-67-AC2.negativeCase: Use a markup-bearing invalid value and assert window.__fixtureExecuted remains absent; warning textContent includes the literal invalid value, not executable markup. Missing/corrupt JSON cannot appear as a healthy empty board.
CS-67-AC2.evidenceArtifact: Future named browser assertions with sanitized warning text, exact canonical counts and absent execution sentinel; source-string presence alone is insufficient.
CS-67-AC2.reviewer: Engineering workflow reviewer and Security reviewer

CS-67-AC3.preconditions: Rendered Engineering summary consumes isolated findings and backlog fixtures.
CS-67-AC3.setup: Provide one OPEN finding for each supported severity, plus CLOSED/FIXED controls and backlog priorities deliberately different from finding counts; repeat with zero open findings.
CS-67-AC3.procedure: Read every summary counter's visible label and number in both fixtures; compare against OPEN findings grouped by KNOWN_SEVERITIES.
CS-67-AC3.assertion: Each supported severity has exactly one '<severity> open findings' counter with the exact OPEN count, including zero. Closed/fixed controls and backlog priorities do not influence finding totals; no supported open severity is omitted.
CS-67-AC3.expectedResult: Operators can distinguish review findings from ticket priorities without invisible open work.
CS-67-AC3.testName: CS67 rendered finding counters cover all severities independently of ticket priorities
CS-67-AC3.fixtures: Synthetic severity census with nonmatching backlog priority distribution and an all-zero control.
CS-67-AC3.negativeCase: Removing one severity counter or renaming it as a ticket-priority count must fail the assertion; unknown severities use AC2's visible error path.
CS-67-AC3.evidenceArtifact: Future named browser assertions of labels and numeric counts; no live or human acceptance claimed.

CS-71-AC1.preconditions: Canonical resume module is loaded with fixed clock and synthetic content only.
CS-71-AC1.setup: Use non-English letter-bearing content, whitespace-only text, and the existing supported English resume fixture.
CS-71-AC1.procedure: Call deriveTitles for each input, then deriveFields for unsupported and English content.
CS-71-AC1.assertion: Unsupported readable content yields status undeterminable and titles []; whitespace yields no-content and titles []; English yields derived with nonempty titles. deriveFields exposes corresponding titlesStatus without dropping the discriminator.
CS-71-AC1.expectedResult: Callers distinguish failed determination from absent content even when both arrays are empty.
CS-71-AC1.testName: carries the status out through deriveFields, where every consumer reads it
CS-71-AC1.fixtures: Existing synthetic RESUME fixture and fixed NOW; no private upload or external inference.
CS-71-AC1.negativeCase: A mutation dropping titlesStatus or replacing undeterminable with no-content must fail; unsupported content is not represented as verified absence of experience.
CS-71-AC1.evidenceArtifact: Future exact-content named Vitest result with assertion count, Node version and exit status; source test existence is not a fresh pass.

CS-71-AC2.preconditions: Existing deriveTitles unit harness runs the positive and regression controls together.
CS-71-AC2.setup: Use 'Ingeniero de software sénior en Acme' plus the existing synthetic second line; English control 'Senior Software Engineer | Acme Corp, Pune'; whitespace control.
CS-71-AC2.procedure: Execute the single named test and inspect its three result assertions; do not split unsupported and English cases into unrelated filtered runs.
CS-71-AC2.assertion: In the same test, unsupported content is undeterminable with []; English is derived with exactly ['Senior Software Engineer']; whitespace is no-content and distinct from undeterminable.
CS-71-AC2.expectedResult: Breaking extraction for every language cannot satisfy this criterion.
CS-71-AC2.testName: distinguishes cannot-read from nothing-to-read, and still reads English
CS-71-AC2.fixtures: The existing synthetic strings in the named test; no real candidate data.
CS-71-AC2.negativeCase: Replacing all deriveTitles results with an empty array must fail the paired English assertion; replacing both empty states with one label must fail the whitespace distinction.
CS-71-AC2.evidenceArtifact: Future single-test result showing all three assertions executed; no fabricated language-support claim.

CS-71-AC3.preconditions: Reviewed baseline derive.ts source at local checkpoint 2c37f25a52d7d4635c5cf7ecc2f0068a0cf9c111 is available.
CS-71-AC3.setup: Extract the ROLE_WORDS declaration and title-recognition imports from baseline and proposed implementation; inspect CS-64's language-policy gate.
CS-71-AC3.procedure: Compare normalized ROLE_WORDS entries and inspect changed derivation code for new translation, language detection or vocabulary branches; combine this with AC2 regression results.
CS-71-AC3.assertion: ROLE_WORDS entries are unchanged; no new language recognizer/provider is introduced under CS-71; only explicit determination status and its propagation are within scope; CS-64 remains the language-policy gate.
CS-71-AC3.expectedResult: Reporting unsupported extraction does not silently authorize language expansion.
CS-71-AC3.testName: CS71 determination status preserves the reviewed title vocabulary boundary
CS-71-AC3.fixtures: Recorded baseline module and proposed source, plus synthetic AC2 strings; the planned contract test does not yet exist.
CS-71-AC3.negativeCase: Adding a new-language role entry or translation dependency must fail scope review even if unit tests pass.
CS-71-AC3.evidenceArtifact: Future named contract check plus content-bound source review identifying baseline and proposed revisions; no runtime/provider activation evidence.
CS-71-AC3.reviewer: Resume domain reviewer and independent scope reviewer

CS-46-AC1.preconditions: Local source commit 154974acc372ee0ec2434c95107e7746ee3c59a7 is available; frozen CS-46 source AC remains unchanged.
CS-46-AC1.setup: Read docs/OWNER-DECISIONS-2026-10-02.md, CS-46 section, alongside the generated CS-46 specification.
CS-46-AC1.procedure: Compare the decision provenance against git show at the recorded commit; inspect matching scope and the reparse clarification in the specification.
CS-46-AC1.assertion: Decision is explicit per-fact exclusion, not always-on supplementary union; reparse cannot silently clear prior rejection; years retains explicit-user-value-wins; no LLM reintroduction. Frozen source AC text is preserved.
CS-46-AC1.expectedResult: Approved owner choice is propagated with exact commit/path/section, without claiming runtime completion or reopening the same choice.
CS-46-AC1.testName: CS46-P01 owner direction and historical AC reconciliation
CS-46-AC1.fixtures: Public repository decision record and frozen backlog only; no real candidate data.
CS-46-AC1.negativeCase: Reject a spec that describes owner choice as undecided or treats reparse as automatic consent.
CS-46-AC1.evidenceArtifact: Redacted reviewer receipt containing source commit, section, reviewed spec content hash and verdict; no runtime or provider evidence claimed.
CS-46-AC1.reviewer: Product Architect and independent specification reviewer

CS-46-AC2.preconditions: Future exclusion contract implemented; isolated database migrated; candidate A and candidate B each have synthetic resume and preferences.
CS-46-AC2.setup: A has resume-derived skill 'TypeScript' and title 'Engineer'; neither is in explicit preferences. A declines both, then performs two searches and reparses a changed resume with equivalent normalized facts. B retains accepted facts.
CS-46-AC2.procedure: Read A's matching context and frozen match evidence after rejection, repeated search and reparse; explicitly restore one fact and search again. Attempt to mutate A's exclusions using B's session.
CS-46-AC2.assertion: Rejected normalized facts contribute zero through all three stages; reparse proposes review without clearing exclusions. Explicit restoration returns only the restored fact. B cannot change A's exclusion state; B's accepted facts remain unaffected. Frozen evidence differentiates accepted/profile/excluded provenance.
CS-46-AC2.expectedResult: Candidate intent persists across searches and changed parse revisions with ownership isolation; restoration is explicit and independently scoped.
CS-46-AC2.testName: persists declined resume facts across searches and reparsing until explicit restoration
CS-46-AC2.fixtures: Synthetic owners A/B, two resume parse revisions, normalized-equivalent skills/titles, fixed job snapshot and scoring clock; no production resumes.
CS-46-AC2.negativeCase: Stale or foreign-owner mutation leaves exclusions unchanged; a new parse revision cannot implicitly restore facts; profile-entered years retains precedence over parsed years.
CS-46-AC2.evidenceArtifact: Future exact-content integration run with named test, Node version, database version, exit code and nonzero pass count; sanitized assertions only.
CS-46-AC2.reviewer: Matching domain reviewer, Security reviewer and QA

CS-46-AC3.preconditions: Approved exclusion implementation contract is available; canonical architecture and matching context documentation exist.
CS-46-AC3.setup: Compare docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and packages/matching/src/context.ts documentation with accepted owner direction; historical v2 path in source AC is treated as preserved evidence, not a required current directory.
CS-46-AC3.procedure: Add a documentation-contract assertion against the actual matching context contract after implementation; independently inspect canonical architecture coverage of accepted/excluded fact precedence and reparse behavior.
CS-46-AC3.assertion: Current docs must not claim always-on union of declined facts or no exclusion mechanism after implementation. They must describe explicit restore, preserved suppression across reparse and explicit-user years precedence; source historical AC text remains unchanged.
CS-46-AC3.expectedResult: Canonical documentation and context contract agree with tested behavior; no obsolete wrapper is recreated to satisfy a historical path.
CS-46-AC3.testName: documents canonical accepted and excluded resume fact precedence
CS-46-AC3.fixtures: Canonical architecture text and context module; synthetic matching-context fixtures only.
CS-46-AC3.negativeCase: Fixture containing 'no per-skill exclusion' as a current contract fails once exclusion implementation is delivered; historical citations remain permitted when explicitly labeled.
CS-46-AC3.evidenceArtifact: Future named contract test result plus content-bound independent documentation review receipt.
CS-46-AC3.reviewer: Matching domain reviewer and Technical Documentation reviewer

CS-40.section: CS-40 / CS-88 — admin authorization and admin UX
CS-40.decision: Dedicated privileged Admin Control Plane with server-enforced RBAC, least privilege, seven approved roles and no arbitrary database editor or secret-bearing UI.
CS-40.remainingGate: Exact permission/projection contracts and independent security/design review. Approval does not prove implementation or authorize unrestricted mutations.

CS-44.decision: No second bespoke email-token recovery system. Carry non-enumeration, expiry, single-use, replay rejection and abuse controls into Cognito; preserve authenticated password change/operator recovery until release.
CS-44.remainingGate: Sender identity/domain evidence and security review; historical registration-disabled AC is the pre-Cognito safety boundary, not a ban on approved Cognito signup.

CS-46.decision: Explicit durable per-fact exclusion gate. Accepted resume facts plus explicit preferences only. Excluded facts contribute zero; reparse creates reviewable proposals without silently clearing candidate intent. Restoration explicit/reversible; provenance visible; explicit user years wins; no LLM reintroduction.
CS-46.remainingGate: Implementation/data contract and tests remain unproven. Historical AC2 'until re-parsed' is a lower bound, not permission to clear exclusions on reparse; later owner direction governs.

CS-88.section: CS-40 / CS-88 — admin authorization and admin UX
CS-88.decision: Admin Control Plane scope approved; imported Design System is visual authority; real redacted API data or honest unavailable states only.
CS-88.remainingGate: Exact per-screen responsive mappings, RBAC/API contracts and actual named independent reviews. Functional approval is not proof every screen is designed.

CS-89.decision: Assistive preparation/explanation approved but production default-OFF; never control deterministic ranking, authorization, identity, verification or application state.
CS-89.remainingGate: Runtime secret, current provider-catalog free-model proof, budget/kill switch, exact-SHA live verification and rollback remain required; no activation in this phase.
